topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecture series, outlines the primary learning objectives, and sets the scope for studying cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer etiology: genetic, environmental, and epidemiological factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the fundamental concepts of cancer development by examining how intrinsic cellular mutations, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures interact to determine cancer risk across populations.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens drive malignant transformation, focusing on the cooperative mechanisms linking Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which environmental, dietary, and occupational mutagens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA lesions and adducts.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of carcinogenesis including inflammatory promotion, signaling pathway activation, and developmental tissue susceptibility, concluding with a synthesis of carcinogenic pathways.

topics.label: Methods for identifying carcinogens and evaluating cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to determine carcinogenicity and assess human exposure risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarises the key takeaways of the lecture and brings the presentation to a close.
